items.followUp: Why are quantitative observations useful in a biological investigation?

rubric.why: Award for stating that quantitative observations use numerical measurements and are precise or accurate.
rubric.description: Numerical measurements are precise or accurate.
rubric.how: Look for a reference to numbers or measurement together with precision or accuracy.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that quantitative data can be analysed or support reliable conclusions.
rubric.description: Quantitative data can be analysed and help produce reliable conclusions.
rubric.how: Look for mathematical or statistical analysis, or reliable conclusions.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations are recorded as numbers using measurements, so they are more precise and objective than qualitative observations.
They can be compared and analysed mathematically, making conclusions more reliable.

items.followUp: State the main principles of cell theory.

rubric.why: Award for stating that organisms are composed of cells and/or that the cell is the basic unit of life.
rubric.description: All living organisms are made of cells; the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
rubric.how: Look for the composition of organisms from cells or the cell being the basic unit.

rubric.why: Award for stating that new cells come from cells that already exist.
rubric.description: All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that cells originate from existing cells.

modelAnswer: All living organisms are made up of one or more cells, and the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
New cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

items.followUp: What is endocytosis? Name its two types.

rubric.why: Award for defining endocytosis as the uptake of material into a cell by the cell membrane enclosing it.
rubric.description: Endocytosis is the intake of substances when the plasma membrane folds around them and forms a vesicle.
rubric.how: Look for uptake into the cell by inward folding or enclosing action of the membrane.

rubric.description: The types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.
rubric.how: Both type names must be present.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which the plasma membrane folds around substances and encloses them in a vesicle to bring them into the cell.
Its two types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

items.followUp: State two aims of biological classification.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the aim of making organisms easier to identify.
rubric.description: Classification helps identify organisms and makes their study easier.
rubric.how: Look for identification or easier study of organisms.

rubric.why: Award for referring to comparing organisms or determining their relationships.
rubric.description: Classification helps show similarities and differences among organisms and their relationships.
rubric.how: Look for comparison of characteristics or evolutionary relationships.

modelAnswer: Classification organizes organisms into groups, making them easier to identify and study.
It helps show similarities and differences among organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: How can community participation help conserve forests and wildlife?

rubric.why: Award for stating the project's role in protecting Himalayan forests or their habitats.
rubric.description: The project helps protect Himalayan forests and wildlife habitats.
rubric.how: Look for protection or conservation of forests or habitats.

rubric.why: Award for mentioning local community involvement or sustainable use as part of conservation.
rubric.description: It promotes conservation through local community involvement and sustainable management.
rubric.how: Look for community participation or sustainable management.

modelAnswer: The Himalayan Jungle Project helps conserve biodiversity by protecting Himalayan forests and the habitats of their wildlife.
It encourages local communities to take part in conservation and sustainable forest management.

items.followUp: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Award for defining aerobic respiration as respiration that uses oxygen and involves complete breakdown of food.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration breaks down food completely in the presence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Look for oxygen and complete breakdown.

rubric.why: Award for defining anaerobic respiration as respiration without oxygen and involving incomplete breakdown of food.
rubric.description: Anaerobic respiration breaks down food incompletely in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Look for absence of oxygen and incomplete breakdown.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the complete breakdown of food in the presence of oxygen to release energy.
Anaerobic respiration is the incomplete breakdown of food in the absence of oxygen to release energy.

items.followUp: Describe how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Award for stating that increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis, at least initially.
rubric.description: Increasing CO₂ concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Look for the rate rising as CO₂ concentration rises.

rubric.why: Award for stating that the increase stops at a limit or the rate levels off when another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.description: At a certain concentration the rate reaches a maximum and levels off because another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Look for a maximum, levelling off, or another limiting factor.

modelAnswer: As CO₂ concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided other factors are not limiting.
The rate eventually reaches a maximum and levels off when another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: Which type of cell division allows an organism to grow and replace damaged cells?

rubric.why: Award both marks for identifying mitosis as the cell division involved in wound healing.
